docs.title: vergil-fixture-ts-lib
docs.text:
A test fixture, not a real library

This package is a Vergil test fixture. It has no users, and it is never published to npm.

vergil-fixture-ts-lib is a small TypeScript library that exists so Vergil's TypeScript support has a real library to work on. Each fixture run makes a small change to it and drives that change through Vergil's whole cycle for real: the PR, CI, the merge, the release and this docs site. A step that breaks shows up here before it reaches a real TypeScript repo.

It exercises:

  • vrg-validate for TypeScript: Prettier, then ESLint, tsc and Vitest from the repo's own node_modules, the build to dist/, the tests at 100% line coverage, and the npm audit and license checks;
  • the CI and release workflows a real TypeScript library gets, with every fleet automation enabled;
  • two real runtime dependencies, zod and change-case, so the audit, the license check and Dependabot have real work to do.

Why the fixtures exist, and how a fixture run works, is set out in the language fixture repos spec.

docs.title: API
docs.text: Everything public is exported from the package's one entry point, vergil-fixture-ts-lib (src/index.ts). The build emits it to dist/, with declaration files beside the JavaScript.

docs.title: greet
docs.text:
function greet(name: string): string;

Greets name, trimmed of surrounding whitespace. A blank name greets the world.

import { greet } from "vergil-fixture-ts-lib";

greet("Ada"); // "Hello, Ada"
greet("  Grace "); // "Hello, Grace"
greet(""); // "Hello, world"

docs.title: parseGreeting and Greeting
docs.text:
function parseGreeting(json: string): Greeting;

interface Greeting {
  readonly name: string;
  readonly punctuation?: string;
}

parseGreeting reads a greeting from a JSON object with a required string name and an optional string punctuation, and trims the name. It checks the object's shape with zod.

import { parseGreeting, renderGreeting } from "vergil-fixture-ts-lib";

const greeting = parseGreeting('{"name": "Ada", "punctuation": "!"}');
renderGreeting(greeting); // "Hello, Ada!"

It throws a GreetingError whose kind is:

  • "json" when the input is not JSON;
  • "shape" when the JSON is not an object, has no string name, has a punctuation that is not a string, or has any other field;
  • "blank-name" when the name is empty or only whitespace.

docs.title: renderGreeting
docs.text:
function renderGreeting(greeting: Greeting): string;

The greeting as text: greet of its name, then its punctuation.

import { renderGreeting } from "vergil-fixture-ts-lib";

renderGreeting({ name: "Ada", punctuation: "!" }); // "Hello, Ada!"
renderGreeting({ name: "Ada" }); // "Hello, Ada"

docs.title: GreetingError and GreetingErrorKind
docs.text:
type GreetingErrorKind = "json" | "shape" | "blank-name";

class GreetingError extends Error {
  readonly kind: GreetingErrorKind;
}

The error parseGreeting throws. kind says why the input was rejected, and cause carries the underlying JSON or zod error where there is one.

docs.title: wordCount
docs.text:
function wordCount(text: string): number;

Counts the whitespace-separated words in text.

import { wordCount } from "vergil-fixture-ts-lib";

wordCount("the quick  brown fox"); // 4
wordCount(""); // 0

docs.title: initials
docs.text:
function initials(text: string): string;

The upper-cased first letter of each whitespace-separated word in text.

import { initials } from "vergil-fixture-ts-lib";

initials("Ada Lovelace"); // "AL"
initials("émilie du châtelet"); // "ÉDC"

docs.title: reverseWords
docs.text:
function reverseWords(text: string): string;

The whitespace-separated words of text in reverse order, joined by single spaces.

import { reverseWords } from "vergil-fixture-ts-lib";

reverseWords("the quick  brown fox"); // "fox brown quick the"
reverseWords("   "); // ""

docs.title: toSlug
docs.text:
function toSlug(text: string): string;

text as a lower-case, hyphen-separated slug, by change-case's kebabCase.

import { toSlug } from "vergil-fixture-ts-lib";

toSlug("Hello, World"); // "hello-world"
toSlug("wordCount"); // "word-count"

docs.title: toIdentifier
docs.text:
function toIdentifier(text: string): string;

text as a camel-case identifier, by change-case's camelCase.

import { toIdentifier } from "vergil-fixture-ts-lib";

toIdentifier("word count"); // "wordCount"
toIdentifier("reverse-words"); // "reverseWords"

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: The package is not on npm (a fixture never reaches a package registry), so work on it from a clone of the repository.

docs.title: Validate
docs.text:
Validation runs in Vergil's TypeScript dev image, the same way CI runs it:

vrg-container-run -- vrg-validate

That installs the locked dependencies, checks formatting and lints, type-checks, builds the library to dist/, runs the tests at 100% line coverage and audits the dependencies. There is no other validation command.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
The build script compiles src/ to dist/, with declaration files and source maps, through tsconfig.build.json:

vrg-container-run -- sh -c "npm ci --ignore-scripts && npm run build"

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
Path What it holds src/index.ts The entry point: the exports that make up the public API src/greeting.ts The greeting functions src/text.ts The text functions src/errors.ts The library's error type tests/ One Vitest file per module tsconfig.json Extends Vergil's managed tsconfig.vergil.json; checks everything tsconfig.build.json The build: src/ only, emitted to dist/ eslint.config.mjs Builds on Vergil's managed eslint.vergil.config.mjs vitest.config.ts Which files the tests and their coverage take in

tsconfig.vergil.json, eslint.vergil.config.mjs and .prettierrc.json are managed by the Vergil fleet sync: never edit them here.

docs.title: Adding a function
docs.text:
Each fixture run adds one function, without restructuring the library:

  1. Write its tests in the tests/ file for its theme, or a new one.
  2. Add the function, with a doc comment, to the module for its theme, or to a new module under src/.
  3. Export it from src/index.ts.
  4. Document it on the API page.
  5. Add it to the function list in README.md.
  6. Run vrg-container-run -- vrg-validate.
